topic_title: Christmas Decor Crafts: 8 Easy DIY Ideas for Your Home
intro: A craft is only worth making if it finishes, so time and materials matter more than ambition. Check three things before you begin. First, how long it takes to dry or bake, since salt dough and orange slices need hours. Second, what the supplies cost, because several of these use things already in a kitchen or a yard. Third, who is around: pets chew string and eat dough, and small children need larger beads and no hot glue.

picks.description: Salt dough is the classic first craft because it uses flour, salt and water already in most kitchens. Mix one cup of flour, half a cup of salt and about half a cup of water, roll to a quarter inch thick, cut with cookie cutters and poke a hole at the top for ribbon. Bake at 200 F for two to three hours until fully dry, or air-dry for a day or two. Thicker shapes take longer, and a soft center is the usual reason ornaments crack later. Paint with acrylics once cool and seal with a clear spray or brush-on sealer so humidity does not soften them. Salt dough is not safe for dogs or cats to eat, so hang the ornaments above pet reach.
picks.best_for: Beginners and families who want a rainy-afternoon craft that lasts for years
picks.skip_if: You have a pet that chews ornaments, since the salt content is harmful to animals
picks.quirky_fact: Salt dough ornaments dated on the back make keepsakes that families often pull out year after year.
picks.product_name: Wooden Round Cookie Cutters Christmas Set

picks.description: Dried orange slices give a garland a warm, translucent glow and a faint scent that fills a room. Slice oranges about a quarter inch thick, blot them with a towel, and bake on a rack at 200 F for roughly three hours, flipping every 30 to 45 minutes, until they feel dry and leathery. Thread with a needle and twine, alternating with cinnamon sticks, bay leaves or wooden beads. A dozen oranges makes around five feet of garland. Slices that are still damp in the middle will mold in storage, so let them cool and dry overnight before stringing. Keep the garland away from damp windows and from hungry pets, and expect it to last one season.
picks.best_for: Mantels, window frames and anyone who likes a natural, scented look
picks.skip_if: You want decor you can reuse for several years, since the slices fade and get brittle
picks.quirky_fact: A bag of oranges costs about the same as a single store-bought garland strand, and yields more length.

picks.description: Pinecones glued in a stack on a cone base make small tabletop trees that work as a grouping of three on a console or a shelf. Start with a foam or cardboard cone, and glue pinecone scales or whole small cones from the bottom up with hot glue. Brush on white paint for a snowy look, or dust with fine glitter while the paint is wet. Bring pinecones inside only after baking them at 200 F for about 30 minutes to kill insects and dry the sap, which also opens the scales. Smaller pinecones from pine and spruce give the neatest result. Use hot glue with care, since the nozzle runs at high heat and children need help.
picks.best_for: Gatherers who can collect pinecones free and want a rustic, low-cost craft
picks.skip_if: You have no safe access to pinecones or are not comfortable using a hot glue gun
picks.quirky_fact: Baking pinecones first opens the scales fully, which makes the finished tree look fuller.
picks.product_name: Styrofoam Cones for Crafts 12 Inch Set

picks.description: A mason jar lantern is quick to make and gives the mantel a steady glow. Brush the outside with white craft glue and roll it in Epsom salt or fake snow for a frosted look, then set a battery tea light inside. Use LED tea lights and not real candles, because glue, salt and paper decoration near a flame is a fire risk. Tie twine or ribbon around the neck and add a sprig of faux pine. Wide-mouth pint jars are simplest because a hand fits inside to place the light. Let the glue dry flat for a few hours before moving them. Frost only the outside, so the light shines through clean glass.
picks.best_for: Anyone wanting an inexpensive, quick craft that also acts as ambient lighting
picks.skip_if: You plan to use real candles, because frosted jars and dried glue are not flame-safe
picks.quirky_fact: Epsom salt works as a cheap, sparkly snow substitute that sticks well to white glue.
picks.product_name: Wide Mouth Mason Jars 16 oz 12 Pack

picks.description: Yarn pom-poms in red, white and green string into a soft, bright garland that suits kids' rooms, mantels and tree branches. A plastic pom-pom maker makes uniform balls in minutes, while a fork or cardboard rings work with no purchase. A 2-inch pom-pom needs roughly two to three yards of yarn. Trim each one into a round shape and thread them onto twine with a needle, spacing about two inches apart. A 6-foot garland takes 25 to 30 pom-poms. Wool and acrylic yarn both work, but acrylic is cheaper and washes easily. Keep it away from candles and fireplaces, since yarn burns quickly, and from pets who like to chew string.
picks.best_for: Craft-minded people who want a soft, colorful garland and enjoy repetitive tasks
picks.skip_if: You have a cat or dog that chews yarn, or you are short on time
picks.quirky_fact: One 100-yard skein of worsted yarn makes about forty 2-inch pom-poms.
picks.product_name: Pom Pom Maker Tool Kit Set

picks.description: Paper snowflakes cost almost nothing and fill a window with white shapes that read from outside. Fold a square of white printer paper into a triangle, then fold twice more, and cut notches along the edges before unfolding. Six-sided snowflakes look the most realistic, and need a square folded in sixths, which takes a bit more practice. Coffee filters work well too and are very easy to cut. Stick them on glass with a small piece of removable tape or a dab of water, which holds paper to glass for a day or two. Press flat under books before hanging to remove the creases.
picks.best_for: Children, classrooms and renters who want zero-cost window decor
picks.skip_if: You want decor that lasts all season, because paper curls in sunlight and humidity
picks.quirky_fact: Real snowflakes have six arms, so paper versions folded into sixths look the most accurate.

picks.description: Wrapping a pillar candle in cinnamon sticks gives a plain candle a spiced, rustic look. Hold the sticks against the candle with rubber bands first, then secure with twine and remove the bands. Use an LED pillar candle, or tall glass-enclosed candles, because the sticks can burn if a flame touches them. Sticks about 3 inches long suit a standard 3-inch pillar. A bundle of 20 sticks wraps one candle fully. Add a sprig of rosemary or a dried orange slice under the twine for color. Cinnamon sticks are inexpensive in bulk bags and dry out safely, which lets you reuse them next year.
picks.best_for: People who like a scented rustic centerpiece and want a ten-minute craft
picks.skip_if: You want a real flame, because dry cinnamon sticks near a wick are a fire risk
picks.quirky_fact: Cassia cinnamon, the type usually sold in grocery stores, has a stronger scent than true Ceylon cinnamon.

picks.description: A wooden bead garland has a simple farmhouse look and holds up from year to year. Thread 16 to 20 mm beads on thick cotton twine or jute with a knot between every few beads. Natural beads give a neutral look, while painted white, red and green beads match more traditional trees. A 6-foot garland needs about 75 to 100 beads of 16 mm. Tie the ends with loops so it hangs on hooks without damage. Hot glue a small bead at the end of the twine to stop beads sliding off. Because the beads are solid, the garland is sturdy enough for stairs, mantels and a tree. Store it coiled in a small box.
picks.best_for: People wanting a durable, reusable farmhouse garland that takes little skill
picks.skip_if: You prefer a bold, glittery look, since natural wood beads are plain on purpose
picks.quirky_fact: Wooden beads in mixed sizes make the garland look handmade rather than store-bought.

faqs.question: What are the easiest Christmas decor crafts for beginners?
faqs.answer: Paper snowflakes, pom-pom garlands and wooden bead garlands need almost no skill, and the supplies are cheap. Salt dough ornaments and mason jar lanterns are slightly more involved but use simple steps. Pick a craft that finishes in one sitting, so the result feels satisfying rather than half-done.

faqs.question: How long do homemade salt dough ornaments last?
faqs.answer: Fully dried and sealed with a clear coat, salt dough ornaments can last for many years. Unsealed ones soften in humid air and may crumble or mold. Store them wrapped in tissue in a cool, dry box. Keep them away from pets, since salt dough is harmful if eaten.

faqs.question: How do I dry orange slices for a garland?
faqs.answer: Slice oranges about a quarter inch thick, blot them dry and bake on a wire rack at 200 F for about three hours, turning every 30 to 45 minutes. They are done when they feel dry and leathery with no wet spots. Let them cool fully before threading. Store them in a dry box and expect them to last a season.

faqs.question: What Christmas crafts are safe for kids?
faqs.answer: Paper snowflakes, pom-poms and bead stringing suit children with an adult nearby. Keep hot glue and the oven for adults, and use blunt-tip scissors for younger children. Small beads are a choking risk for toddlers, so choose larger ones. Salt dough should be supervised, because children can taste it.

faqs.question: How can I make Christmas crafts look less homemade?
faqs.answer: Limit the palette to two or three colors, use even spacing, and finish with a good ribbon or twine. Natural materials like wood, pinecones and dried fruit look polished together. Display crafts in groups of three rather than scattering them, and keep them off cluttered surfaces.

seo_title: Christmas Decor Crafts: 8 Easy DIY Ideas for 2026
answer: Salt dough ornaments are the best first craft, followed by a dried orange slice garland and pinecone mini trees. The deciding factor is who is making them: paper snowflakes and pom-poms suit children, while the oven-based crafts need an adult.
method: Picked from Pinterest's trending searches for Christmas decor crafts, then ordered by how few supplies each needs, how quickly it finishes and how well the result holds up through December.
